hook: The first Christian emperor, who founded Constantinople.

pages.x: Constantine was born around 272 at Naissus, in what is now Serbia, son of a Roman officer, Constantius, and Helena, a woman of humble birth. He grew up at the court of Emperor Diocletian, almost a hostage, while his father rose to rule the western empire.
When his father died at York in 306, the soldiers proclaimed Constantine emperor. The empire was then split between several rival emperors, and it took him 18 years of war to beat them all.
pages.cap: York, where his soldiers hailed him

pages.x: Before a battle for Rome in 312, Constantine said he saw a cross of light in the sky with the words "In this sign, conquer". He had his soldiers paint a Christian symbol on their shields, and beat his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge, where Maxentius drowned in the Tiber.

In 313, with his fellow emperor Licinius, he issued the Edict of Milan, letting everyone worship as they wished and giving back property taken from Christians. Only ten years earlier, Diocletian had been burning churches and killing Christians.

In 325 he called bishops from all over the empire to Nicaea to settle a bitter quarrel about whether Jesus was equal to God the Father. The Nicene Creed they agreed on is still said in churches every Sunday.

In 330 he made the old Greek town of Byzantium his new capital, New Rome. Everyone called it Constantinople, "the city of Constantine". It stayed the capital of the Roman, then Byzantine, Empire for 1,100 years, and is now Istanbul.

He put off being baptised until he was dying, in 337, perhaps so that the sins of a lifetime as emperor would be washed away all at once. He was buried among memorials to the twelve apostles, as if he were the thirteenth.
Constantine was the first Christian emperor, and he set Christianity on its way to becoming the religion of Europe. His city carried the Roman Empire on in the east for over a thousand years.
